newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt tracks U.S. Treasuries lower.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt tracks U.S. Treasuries lower.

text.p: Emerging debt prices drifted lower in line with U.S. Treasuries on Monday, traders said.
As in the past, par bonds took a heavier beating than other Brady debt, but Brazil "C" bond was also notably weaker, which traders attributed to the lack of progress in social security reform.
"The Congress is going on recess at the end of month," said a trader. "Nothing's going to happen."
Thomas Trebat, head of emerging markets research at Citicorp Securities, agreed that the halting pace of reform was wearing down the patience of market participants.

While Brazil's privatization was on track with the balance of payments improving, a stronger momentum on the social security front was needed in the second half of the year to get skeptics off the sidelines, he said.
Brazil C lost 7/8 at 80-5/8 bid. Brazil Global 27 fell 1-1/8 at 96-3/8.
Mexico assets underformed other Latin debt as pre-election jitters took a toll, traders said.
UMS-26 fell 1-1/2 to 114-1/4, and Mexico Pars lost 1-1/8 at 77-7/8.

The death of Mexico's long-time labor leader, Fidel Velazquez, at age 97 on Saturday focused people's attention on the future of Mexico's union movement, which, together with other changes the coming elections may bring to the country, appeared somewhat unsettling, Trebat said.
"There is going to be a sea change in Mexican politics," he said. "The market so far has not fully discounted all those factors."
With the Institutional Revolutionary Party set to lose the majority in the parliament and the mayorty of the Mexico City, how the new "power-sharing" works is an open question, he noted.
Overall for the emerging markets, traders remained fairly upbeat, noting that inflow of funds continued to be strong last week.
"There are not many events-driven trades," said a trader.
But as long as the long bond stayed at the current level, the emerging markets would be all right, he said.
The benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 17/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
